args.summary: The data had several issues affecting the average body mass by sex. There was one exact duplicate row (row 34) which the user chose not to remove. Species names had trailing/leading spaces (e.g., 'Adelie ', ' Gentoo') which were safely normalized. The sex column had 'MALE' in uppercase which was normalized to 'male'. Most critically, three body mass values (rows 21, 30, 41) were grossly out of range (millions of grams instead of thousands), but the user rejected their exclusion. The analysis used 41 rows (3 missing sex values were excluded). The resulting averages are highly skewed: female ~153,726g and male ~639,471g. These values are not biologically plausible and are due to the uncorrected data errors. The correct averages cannot be computed without fixing the body mass errors.
